entities.summary:
Hellanicus of Mytilene was a prominent ancient Greek logographer who lived during the latter half of the 5th century BC. He was born on the island of Lesbos, which was a major cultural and intellectual center of the ancient Greek world.

As a logographer, Hellanicus was known for his work in the field of genealogy, and his writings were highly regarded by his contemporaries.

Hellanicus' significance extends beyond his own lifetime, as his work helped to shape our understanding of ancient Greek history and culture.

The exact dates of Hellanicus' birth and death are unknown, but it is believed that he lived from around 450 to 404 BCE.

A significant example of Hellanicus' work is his book on the history of the Mytilenian people, which provides valuable insights into the culture and politics of the region.

This work is significant because it was one of the first attempts to chronicle the history of the Mytilenian people, and it helped to establish the importance of genealogy in understanding ancient Greek society.

The legacy of Hellanicus can be seen in the work of later logographers, who built upon his research and further developed the field of genealogy in ancient Greece.

In conclusion, Hellanicus of Mytilene was a significant figure in the history of ancient Greece, and his work continues to be studied by scholars today.

Hellanicus' contribution to the field of genealogy can be seen in the following quote: "The historian must be a genealogist, for he must trace the line of descent from the earliest times to the present day."
